chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindy, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The few initiate the many with the greeting (salam), and the rider initiates the walker, and the riders of mules initiate the riders of donkeys, and the riders of horses initiate the riders of mules.

key_terms.الرَّاكِب: One mounted on an animal (horse, mule, donkey) — contrasted with the pedestrian
key_terms.السَّلَام: The Islamic greeting of peace (Assalamu Alaykum), both the greeting itself and the obligation to initiate it
key_terms.الْبِغَال: Mules (plural of baghl) — considered of intermediate status between horses and donkeys
key_terms.الْخَيْل: Horses — considered the noblest riding animal, whose riders greet those on mules
key_terms.يَبْدَأُ / يَبْدَءُونَ: To initiate, to begin — referring specifically to who should begin the greeting first

ai.seo_question: Who is supposed to initiate the salam greeting according to Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchy for who bears the obligation to begin the Islamic greeting of salam. In classical Islamic social etiquette, initiating the salam was considered an act of humility and courtesy. The Imam specifies four cases: the minority greets the majority, the mounted greets the pedestrian, the mule-rider greets the donkey-rider, and the horse-rider greets the mule-rider — reflecting a status-based protocol where the one of higher status or mobility initiates.
